newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa wage talks fail, strike imminent.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa wage talks fail, strike imminent.

text.p: The DAG union representing white-collar workers at German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Tuesday its members were poised to strike on Thursday after wage talks ended without result on late Monday.
"There will be a strike," a member of the DAG's negotiating team told Reuters.
The strike was certain to hit Frankfurt airport, the country's biggest and Hamburg was also likely to be affected, the official said.
Early Tuesday morning, the DAG announced that its talks with Lufthansa aimed at reaching a wages deal by mid-week had ended without result late on Monday.
The union said Lufthansa's management board had refused to offer workers a wage contract with one year's validity and of a "volume normal for the sector".
Given the threat that many Lufthansa jobs could be moved abroad, the union would not tie itself to a two-year contract, the DAG said.

DAG represents the airline's pilots, flight attendants and other white collar workers. Other staff are represented by the OeTV union, which has agreed a wage deal with Lufthansa that the DAG rejected.
